title: HMDA home-purchase micro-markets by census tract, county subdivision (CCD) and place, Hawaii, 2025 (2019 comparison)

hmda.publisher: FFIEC / CFPB HMDA Data Browser API (loan-level CSV, already downloaded for an/new/hmda.json)

census_geography.publisher: U.S. Census Bureau, www2.census.gov (TIGER/Line 2020 and 2010 faces and blocks, 2020 Gazetteer, 2020 and 2010 Block Assignment Files)

source.scripts: pull/gap_hmda_tract/: download.sh, extract.py, dbf.py, crosswalk.py (tract -> CCD/place/ZCTA), analyze.py (aggregation), finalize.py (this file), verify.py (independent pandas recomputation)

method: Universe = an/new/hmda.json: action_taken=1 (originated), loan_purpose=1 (home purchase), construction_method=1 (site-built), total_units 1-4. All lien positions kept (n_first_lien also given). 2025: 9,875 loans; 2019: 13,797.
HMDA census_tract (11-digit GEOID) is 2020-vintage for 2025 data and 2010-vintage for 2019 data. Two crosswalks were built.

Tract -> county subdivision (CCD): Hawaii Block Assignment Files have no CCD file, so each census block was assigned its CCD (COUSUBFP) and place (PLACEFP) from TIGER/Line topological faces (2020 faces for 2020 blocks; 2010 faces COUSUBFP10/PLACEFP10 for 2010 blocks). Blocks were weighted by census housing units (2020 HOUSING20 from tl_2020_15_tabblock20; 2010 HOUSING10 from tabblock2010_15_pophu). A tract is assigned to the CCD holding the most of its housing units.

Tracts nest in CCDs almost everywhere: in 2020 only 6 of 461 tracts span CCDs, 4 of them water/offshore tracts (99xxxx) with no 2025 loans. The two land splits are 15009031900 (Kahului 87% / Spreckelsville 13% of housing units; 14 loans in 2025, assigned to Kahului CCD) and 15009032000 (Kihei 56% / Lahaina 44%; Maalaea-Launiupoko area; 11 loans in 2025, assigned to Kihei CCD). The 2020 place assignment from faces matched the 2020 Block Assignment File INCPLACE_CDP for all 14,732 blocks.

CCD codes and names are identical in the 2010 and 2020 vintages (44 CCDs), so CCD-level 2019 vs 2025 comparisons are like-for-like geographies; tract-level results are NOT comparable across years (different tract vintages).

Place group: all Hawaii places are CDPs (no incorporated places). A tract is labeled with the CDP holding >=60% of its housing units; otherwise with the CDPs holding >=20% joined by "/" and marked "(mixed tract)" (a single name with "(mixed tract)" means the rest of the tract lies outside that CDP); otherwise "<CCD>, outside a single CDP". Place groups are tract approximations of CDPs, not exact CDP totals, and a CDP can appear under two CCDs (e.g. Wailea CDP under Kihei CCD and Kula CCD).
ZCTA group: each tract is assigned to the ZIP Code Tabulation Area holding >=50% of its 2020 housing units (from the 2020 faces ZCTA5CE20). Approximate; ZCTAs are not exact USPS ZIP delivery areas.
Island: Maui County split into Maui, Molokai (East/West Molokai CCDs) and Lanai (Lanai CCD); Kauai County CCDs other than Niihau = Kauai.

Metrics per group: n_loans, n_first_lien; occupancy shares (principal / second home / investment; second+investment combined also for first liens only); loan type shares (conventional / FHA / VA / USDA); median applicant income (thousands USD, all numeric incomes) and for owner-occupant first liens; median, p25, p75 property value; median first-lien loan amount; share with non-natural-person applicant (applicant_age 8888) and business-purpose share. Medians use linear interpolation (numpy default), as in an/new/hmda.json.

Tract tables list only tracts with >=20 loans (2025: 153 tracts). CCD, place, ZCTA and island tables include every group; groups with n_loans < 20 carry low_n_flag=true, and low_n_fields lists medians computed on fewer than 20 values. Highlights rank only groups with n_loans >= 20.

independent_recompute.method: pandas read of raw CSV, same filters, numpy median; compared with data.years.<y>.by_ccd and by_tract_n_ge_20

notes: Aggregates only. No borrower, owner, street address or parcel information is used or output; census tract GEOIDs and ZCTA codes are public statistical areas.

Unit = HMDA loan record, not a property sale. Cash purchases are absent from HMDA, so shares describe financed purchases only; resort areas with many cash buyers are under-represented in counts and the true non-owner share of all buyers there is not measured here.

Second-home vs investment coding shifted between 2019 and 2025 (see an/new/hmda.json notes; four-county second-home share 9.1% -> 4.9%, investment 12.0% -> 16.5%). Use share_second_plus_investment for comparisons; the split is lender-reported.

Income = income relied on for credit, thousands USD, nominal. It is NA for 645 of 9,875 loans in 2025 (many investor/business-purpose and non-natural-person loans), so income medians in investor-heavy areas describe the subset of loans with reported income. Second-home and investor buyers often live off-island; their incomes describe the buyer, not local residents.
Property value and loan amount are $10k-bin midpoints in public HMDA. 134 of 9,875 2025 loans lack a usable property value.
Waikiki-area tracts (ZCTA 96815) include condo-hotel and condominium stock; high investment shares there reflect property type as well as buyer type.
VA share counts VA-guaranteed loans among all purchase loans in the area; it is a proxy for active-duty/veteran buyers, not a count of military households.
Lahaina CCD 2025 counts are post-August-2023 wildfire; low counts in Lahaina-town tracts reflect destroyed stock. No causal analysis was done.
Small islands: Molokai (27 loans in 2025) and Lanai (5) are reported at island level; their CCD and tract cells are all n<20 and flagged.
Hawaii County has 1 loan with census_tract NA: included in county totals only.
